tools.name: create_inbox
tools.description: Create a webhook inbox. Returns its ingest URL and a read token (shown once).

tools.name: wait_for_event
tools.description: Wait for the next event in an inbox after a cursor, up to 30s. Auth: Authorization Bearer read token header.

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: List events in an inbox. Auth: Authorization Bearer read token header.

tools.name: get_event
tools.description: Get one event by id. Auth: Authorization Bearer read token header.

tools.name: extract_field
tools.description: Pull a JSON path out of an event body. Auth: Authorization Bearer read token header.

tools.name: delete_inbox
tools.description: Delete an inbox and its events. Auth: Authorization Bearer read token header.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_inbox, wait_for_event, list_events, delete_inbox · Private data: create_inbox, wait_for_event, list_events, get_event, extract_field, delete_inbox · Public sink: create_inbox · Destructive: delete_inbox.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_inbox, wait_for_event, list_events, delete_inbox · Private data: create_inbox, wait_for_event, list_events, get_event, extract_field, delete_inbox · Public sink: create_inbox · Destructive: delete_inbox

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
